gate: REH14 manifest re-read cost with the tray and the map open; offline unit checks, no runtime gate passed

fact.map: apps/studio/src/features/map/surface/useSurfaceLayer.ts:31-32 (at 6323b054): each case of the area subscribes through caseSubscriptions.subscribe, and refresh ignores its itemId and calls client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['intake', caseId] }), so every change re-reads the whole manifest (and, being a default invalidate, cancels a manifest read in flight and starts it again)
fact.tray: apps/studio/src/features/intake/BatchPage.tsx:41 (at 6323b054): useMemo(() => new IntakeItemRefresh(client, caseId)), its own TR1 object; a change naming a held item reads that item alone
fact.transport: apps/studio/src/features/intake/case-subscription.ts:97 hands each change to every consumer of the case in one synchronous loop (consumer.refresh(next.itemId)); :78 and :133 call refresh() without an item for the quiet tick and the 409 resync
fact.cost: with the tray and the map open, one item change gave one item read plus one whole manifest read; REH14 timed manifest reads at 15 to 37 s under load

change.registry: itemRefreshFor(client, caseId) in apps/studio/src/features/intake/item-refresh.ts: a WeakMap of QueryClient to a Map of caseId to one IntakeItemRefresh; an entry lives as long as its client, nothing is released while a consumer is mounted
change.tray: BatchPage.tsx useBatchFacts takes itemRefreshFor(client, caseId) instead of its own new IntakeItemRefresh; its words, its others() reads (recipes, package summary) and its full refresh() are unchanged
change.map: useSurfaceLayer passes the change's itemId to itemRefreshFor(client, caseId).changed(itemId); a change without an item, or for an item the cache does not hold, still re-reads the whole manifest by TR1/ZP2's rereadQuery
change.same_turn: IntakeItemRefresh.whole() now asks for one manifest read per turn (a microtask flag): the two consumers of one notification each call it in the same synchronous loop, and before this both calls reached rereadQuery, whose ZP2 rule saw the first read in flight and asked for one more after it (2 manifest reads; measured by the new test against the old code). A change in a later turn while that read is in flight still asks for one more read after it (ZP2 unchanged, tested)
change.react_query_dedupe: checked: react-query dedupes concurrent fetches of one key (invalidateQueries with cancelRefetch:false joins the fetch in flight), but ZP2's rereadQuery deliberately asks for a second read when one is in flight, so dedupe alone gave 2 manifest reads for one change without an item; the same-turn flag gives 1

tray_difference: one, and only in the tray-alone edge where two changes without an item reach the tray in one synchronous turn (for example two frames parsed from one chunk): before, a manifest read plus one more after it; now one manifest read, which began after both notifications were received. Every word and every other behaviour of the tray is unchanged
